points.description: The answer identifies abstraction as a main advantage of object-oriented programming, conveying that it hides complex internal detail behind a simpler interface so the programmer works with essential features. Equivalent wording such as 'hiding complexity' earns the mark.

The answer identifies reusability as a main advantage of object-oriented programming, conveying that classes or objects can be reused in other programs or parts of a program instead of rewriting code. Equivalent wording such as 'code reuse' earns the mark.

rubric.notes: Each of the two named advantages is worth half the total, since the model answer gives exactly these two and neither is more central. Full marks require both advantages to be named with the correct meaning; equivalent wording is accepted. A student who names only one advantage, correctly explained, earns 2.5 out of 5. A bare term with no sense of what it means, or a wrong meaning, earns no credit for that point.
